newsitem.title: USA: Mubarak disappointed at level of U.S. investments.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak disappointed at level of U.S. investments.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Thursday he was disappointed that economic reforms in his country have not produced a higher level of private investment from the United States.
"I must tell you in all candor that the investments of U.S. companies in Egypt is still disappointing," he said.
"The private sectors of our two countries must play a prominent role in our financial relations," he added. "They must provide the initiative and the fighting spirit."

Mubarak, in the final public appearance of his six-day visit to the United States, made the comments to a Chicago audience that included many business leaders, among them the president of Amoco Corp., the largest U.S. investor in Egypt.
Mubarak said the Egyptian economy was at a crossroads, with structural reforms implemented.
"Anyone who has not seen Egypt in the past few months has not seen Egypt," he said. "We have just begun reaping what we have sown."
Egypt's budget deficit at less than 1 percent of gross national product is not a passing phenomenon but "one that can be repeated year after year, well into the next century." he said.
There is an "unshakeable commitment to reform" that has produced a 4.5 percent growth rate that may reach 78 percent by the end of the century, Mubarak said.
Meanwhile, he said his county was "working day and night" to help assure peace in the Middle East.
